correctness.rationale: An LD set meeting both bipartition shores can omit at most one vertex in each shore, as missing same-shore vertices otherwise have equal nonempty traces; one-shore LD sets require that shore be complete and opposite shore be a singleton. Two withheld same-shore vertices construct a universal three-block coalition partition when order>=3. Any pair of coalition blocks leaves at most two outside vertices, bounding size<=4, and a four-block partition forces both outside blocks to be opposite-shore singletons; their required alternate coalition partners force m=n=2. The four singleton blocks in C4 work; in K2 every singleton is already LD, hence no such partition. Own exhaustive small graph partition tests agree, but general result follows from structural argument.
